Exercise A

Comparatives and superlatives

Use -er / -est for short adjectives and more / most for long ones. Remember good → better → best. Choose the correct form for each gap.

Before you start — optional, not marked
This is just to get you thinking. You can leave it empty and it does not count towards your score.
Twelve moments from student life

1. The flat near the station is 1 (cheap) than the flat in the city centre.

2. Online lectures are 2 (convenient) than lectures on campus.

3. Of all the vocabulary apps I have tried, this is the 3 (good).

4. Our new flat is not as 4 (quiet) as the old one.

5. The more I practise, the 5 (easy) it gets.

6. Her presentation was 6 (good) than mine, so her group won.

7. Of the three modules this term, Business English is the 7 (useful).

8. Prices in Munich are a lot 8 (high) than in Leipzig.

9. This café is the 9 (noisy) place on campus, so I never study there.

10. Student flats in this city are getting 10 (expensive) every year.

11. This time yesterday, we 11 (look) at flats in the city centre.

12. Would it be possible 12 move the viewing to Friday?

Exercise B

Compare and recommend

Work with your group in your breakout room. Choose what you are comparing, plan together, then each person types the text here. At 19:30 one group presents its recommendation to the class.

Word count: 0

Write 6–8 sentences. Use at least two comparatives (cheaper than…), one superlative (the best…) and finish with a clear recommendation (So I would choose…).
